quickstart.title: Quickstart: signup to first call
quickstart.description: Create your account, provision a phone number, and answer your first inbound call in under 10 minutes.

body.0: This quickstart walks you through everything you need to take your first live call on QVO. By the end you will have a tenant, an agent, a phone number, and a recorded test conversation.

1.caption: A short walkthrough of the steps below — signup, templates, demo, and live call panels.

3.0: Visit the signup page and enter your business email, company name, and a password.
3.1: Confirm your email by clicking the link we send you.
3.2: Choose your plan (Free Trial works for everything in this guide).

body.5: Your tenant environment is provisioned automatically — no waiting for sales or onboarding calls.
body.7: On first login the onboarding wizard offers pre-tuned agent templates. Pick the one closest to your business; you can change it later.

8.0: Medical / Dental — patient intake, appointment booking, urgent triage
8.1: Legal — new matter intake, conflict checks, callback scheduling
8.2: Home services — dispatch, quote requests, after-hours emergencies
8.3: General business — receptionist, call routing, voicemail capture

11.0: Go to Phone Numbers → Add Number.
11.1: Choose a local or toll-free number.
11.2: Assign it to the agent you just created.

body.13: Number provisioning typically completes in under 30 seconds. Your number is immediately routable.
body.15: Call the number from your phone. The agent will greet you using the template prompt. Speak naturally — interruptions, pauses, and "uhms" are handled.
body.18: Open the Conversations page. You will see your call with a full transcript, the recording, the tools the agent invoked, and a quality score.

0.fix: Check that the agent is published (not draft). Drafts are not assigned to live numbers.

1.fix: Verify your account has voice credits. New trial accounts get 30 minutes free.

2.fix: Open the number, scroll to Routing, and select an agent.

core-concepts.title: Core concepts
core-concepts.description: Tenants, agents, numbers, workflows, and tools — the building blocks of QVO.

body.1: A tenant is your isolated workspace. All calls, agents, numbers, contacts, and integrations belong to exactly one tenant. Row-level security guarantees no data crosses tenant boundaries.
body.3: An agent is the AI that answers (or places) a call. It has a system prompt, a voice, a set of allowed tools, and routing rules. Agents are versioned — every published change creates a new version you can roll back to.
body.5: A SIP/PSTN number we provision on your behalf. Numbers are assigned to agents. One agent can hold many numbers; one number maps to exactly one agent at a time.
body.7: A workflow is a deterministic, multi-step state machine that runs around the agent — for example: identify caller → check calendar → book appointment → send SMS confirmation.
body.9: Tools are the typed function calls an agent can make during a conversation. Examples: lookup_contact, create_ticket, schedule_appointment, transfer_to_human.
body.11: Per-tenant document store the agent can search at runtime. Upload PDFs, URLs, or paste text. Documents are chunked, embedded, and surfaced when the agent needs them.

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.description: Definitions for terms you will see across the product and these docs.

0.0: AMD — Answering Machine Detection. Used in outbound campaigns to skip or leave voicemail.
0.1: BYOC — Bring Your Own Carrier. Use your own SIP trunk instead of QVO-provisioned numbers.
0.2: DNC — Do Not Call. Suppressions enforced before any outbound dial.
0.3: DTMF — Touch-tone digits. Captured as tool input during a call.
0.4: PHI — Protected Health Information. Auto-redacted from transcripts when the HIPAA add-on is enabled.
0.5: RBAC — Role-Based Access Control. Owner, Manager, Member, Viewer.
0.6: RLS — Row-Level Security. Database-enforced tenant isolation.
0.7: TTFB — Time To First Byte. The latency from caller stops talking to agent starts speaking.

building-your-first-agent.title: Building your first agent
building-your-first-agent.description: Write a system prompt, pick a voice, and configure tools and escalations.

body.1: From the Agents page click an agent (or "New Agent"). The builder splits into Identity, Behavior, Tools, Routing, and Test panels.
body.5: The prompt is plain English. Be specific about tone, what to collect, what to refuse, and when to escalate.
body.7: Keep prompts under ~600 words. Longer prompts increase latency and reduce instruction-following.
body.9: Preview voices with a sample sentence. Match the voice to the audience — calm/measured for healthcare, warm for hospitality, energetic for sales.
body.12: Toggle the tools your agent is allowed to call. Each tool has a JSON schema; the agent only sees tools you enable.

15.0: Escalation — keywords or intents that transfer the call to a human.
15.1: Voicemail — what to do when no human is available.
15.2: Post-call — webhooks, SMS confirmations, ticket creation.

body.17: Use the "Test Call" button in the builder to call yourself. Iterate on the prompt until edge cases behave correctly. Most teams ship after 3–5 iterations.

0.problem: Agent ignores parts of the prompt.
0.fix: Number your instructions and put critical ones first. Long unstructured prose is followed less reliably.

1.fix: Add a "if you do not know, say so and offer a callback" clause.

2.fix: Lower interruption sensitivity in Behavior settings.

voice-and-personality.title: Voice and personality
voice-and-personality.description: Tune voice, pacing, fillers, interruption behavior, and pick the right voice for each language.

body.1: Voices vary by gender, accent, age, and energy. Each voice has a latency profile — faster voices feel more natural over the phone.
body.3: All eleven OpenAI voices can speak any language QVO supports, but some sound noticeably more natural than others depending on the language. The Voice & Agent Config panel filters the dropdown into two groups based on the language you selected:

4.0: ★ Recommended — voices tuned for the active language. They appear under a "Recommended for <Language>" group and are starred so they're easy to spot.
4.1: Other voices — still selectable, but grouped under "Other voices (may sound less natural)" so admins know quality may suffer.

body.5: If you pick a voice that is not in the recommended group, the panel highlights the dropdown in amber and shows an inline warning suggesting better alternatives — no save is blocked, but you have an explicit heads-up before publishing.
body.6: When you change the language, the existing voice is kept if it is still in the recommended set. Otherwise the warning appears so you can pick a better-matched voice before publishing.

8.0: English (en) — alloy, ash, ballad, coral, echo, fable, onyx, nova, sage, shimmer, verse (all voices work well).
8.1: Spanish (es) — coral, nova, shimmer, sage, alloy, verse.
8.2: French (fr) — nova, shimmer, sage, alloy, coral, verse.
8.3: German (de) — alloy, nova, sage, shimmer, verse.
8.4: Portuguese (pt) — nova, shimmer, alloy, coral, sage.
8.5: Italian (it) — nova, shimmer, sage, alloy, coral, verse.

body.9: Asian and Arabic-language voices are limited to alloy, nova, and shimmer because the other voices have noticeable English accents in those languages. We refresh the recommendations as OpenAI ships voice updates.

11.1: Pause length controls silence between sentences.
11.2: Filler words ("um", "let me check") humanize transitions.

body.13: Sensitivity 0 means the agent never yields; 1 means any sound interrupts it. 0.5 is the default and works for most settings.

tools-and-functions.title: Tools and functions
tools-and-functions.description: Give your agent typed actions: lookups, bookings, escalations, and custom HTTP.

1.0: lookup_contact — search the CRM by phone or email.
1.1: schedule_appointment — book a slot on a connected calendar.
1.2: create_ticket — open a helpdesk ticket with priority.
1.3: send_sms — text the caller during or after the call.
1.4: transfer_to_human — warm or cold transfer to a configured destination.

body.3: Define a tool with a name, description, JSON schema, and an HTTPS endpoint. Calls are signed and retried on 5xx.

workflows-overview.title: Workflows overview
workflows-overview.description: How deterministic flows complement the LLM and remove ambiguity from critical steps.

body.0: Workflows are deterministic state machines that wrap an agent. Use them when a sequence must happen in a fixed order or when you need explicit branching the LLM should not improvise.
body.1: When to use a workflow

2.2: After-call automations (CRM update, SMS confirmation, ticket).

4.1: Steps — agent_say, tool_call, condition, http_request, wait.
4.2: Transitions — guarded by conditions on collected data.

configuring-workflows.title: Configuring workflows
configuring-workflows.description: Build, version, and publish a workflow attached to an agent.

1.1: Pick a starting trigger (most common: call.started).
1.2: Drag steps onto the canvas and connect them.
1.3: Use the side panel to configure each step.

body.5: Save creates a draft. Publish promotes a draft to production. Previous versions remain available — you can roll back at any time.
body.7: Use the Workflow Simulator to step through with synthetic input before publishing.

integrations-overview.description: How QVO connects to your existing CRM, calendar, helpdesk, and messaging tools.

body.0: Integrations let your agent read and write data in your existing systems during a call. Open Integrations in the sidebar to browse the catalog.
body.1: Authentication
body.2: Most integrations use OAuth — click Connect, sign in to the provider, and grant the requested scopes. API-key based integrations prompt you for the key inline.

4.0: Read — agent looks up the caller in your CRM.
4.1: Write — agent creates a record (contact, ticket, appointment).
4.2: Sync — periodic background sync of mutable data.

body.6: All connection credentials are encrypted at rest. Tokens are scoped per tenant and never exposed to the agent prompt.

connecting-salesforce.title: Connecting Salesforce
connecting-salesforce.description: Create a Salesforce Connected App and authorize QVO to log calls against Contacts, Leads, and Opportunities.

body.0: QVO uses Salesforce OAuth 2.0 with a refresh token so calls can keep syncing in the background. Before you click Connect, your Salesforce admin needs to create a Connected App in your org so QVO has a Client ID and Client Secret to authorize against.
body.1: You only need to do this once per Salesforce org. After the Connected App is created, every QVO tenant admin in your org can connect by signing in.
body.2: 1. Create a Connected App in Salesforce

3.0: In Salesforce, open Setup and search for "App Manager", then click New Connected App.
3.1: Pick "Create a Connected App" and give it a name like "QVO Voice Agent" with your admin contact email.
3.2: Under API (Enable OAuth Settings), check "Enable OAuth Settings".
3.3: Set the Callback URL to https://app.qvo.ai/api/connectors/oauth/salesforce/callback (use your tenant's app domain if you self-host).
3.4: Add the OAuth scopes: api (Manage user data via APIs), refresh_token, offline_access — all three are required.
3.5: Leave "Require Secret for Web Server Flow" and "Require Secret for Refresh Token Flow" enabled.
3.6: Save the app. Salesforce warns it can take up to 10 minutes to propagate.

body.7: After saving, click Manage Consumer Details to copy the Consumer Key (Client ID) and Consumer Secret (Client Secret). You will paste these into QVO.
body.9: QVO points at the standard Salesforce login URL by default (https://login.salesforce.com). For sandbox orgs you must tell us to use the test login host instead by setting the SALESFORCE_LOGIN_URL environment variable on the server.

10.0: Production org → leave SALESFORCE_LOGIN_URL unset (defaults to https://login.salesforce.com).
10.1: Sandbox org (e.g. mycompany--dev.sandbox.my.salesforce.com) → set SALESFORCE_LOGIN_URL=https://test.salesforce.com so QVO authorizes against the sandbox login host.

body.11: If you self-host QVO, set SALESFORCE_LOGIN_URL in your server environment. On Replit Deployments, add it under Secrets. Cloud QVO tenants can request a sandbox toggle by contacting support — include your Salesforce org ID.
body.12: A common failure mode is connecting a sandbox org with SALESFORCE_LOGIN_URL unset. The OAuth flow appears to succeed, then refresh tokens fail silently with invalid_grant. Always verify the login host matches the org type.

14.0: In QVO, go to Integrations → Salesforce → Connect.
14.1: Sign in with the Salesforce account that should own logged calls (a service user is recommended).
14.2: Approve the api, refresh_token, and offline_access scopes when prompted.
14.3: You will be redirected back to QVO with the integration marked Connected.

body.17: Trigger a test call or click "Sync now" on the Salesforce integration card. You should see a Task created on the matching Contact or Lead with the AI call summary in the description.

0.fix: Re-check the Consumer Key was copied without trailing whitespace, and that 10 minutes have passed since you saved the Connected App.

1.fix: Confirm SALESFORCE_LOGIN_URL matches the org type (login.salesforce.com vs test.salesforce.com) and that offline_access is in the scope list.

2.problem: Calls not appearing on Contact timeline.
2.fix: Check the service user has Edit access on Tasks and on the relevant Contact/Lead record types.

3.fix: In Salesforce Setup → Manage Connected Apps → QVO, set IP Relaxation to "Relax IP restrictions" so refresh tokens survive infrastructure changes.

body.21: For deeper detail on Connected Apps see the official Salesforce help: https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.connected_app_create.htm.

connecting-outlook.title: Connecting Outlook Calendar
connecting-outlook.description: Register a Microsoft Entra app and authorize QVO to read availability and book appointments on your Microsoft 365 calendar.

body.0: The Outlook Calendar connector talks to Microsoft Graph using OAuth 2.0 with a refresh token. To get started, an Entra (formerly Azure AD) admin needs to register an app in your tenant so QVO has a Client ID, Client Secret, and tenant ID to authorize against.
body.1: App registration is a one-time job per Microsoft 365 tenant. Once it is in place, every QVO user in your org can connect their own calendar by signing in.
body.2: 1. Register an app in Microsoft Entra

3.0: Go to https://entra.microsoft.com → Applications → App registrations → New registration.
3.1: Name it something like "QVO Voice Agent".
3.2: Under Supported account types choose "Accounts in this organizational directory only" for single-tenant, or "Accounts in any organizational directory" for multi-tenant.
3.3: Set the Redirect URI to Web → https://app.qvo.ai/api/connectors/oauth/outlook/callback (use your own app domain if you self-host).
3.4: Click Register. Copy the Application (client) ID and the Directory (tenant) ID from the Overview page.

7.0: Open the app registration → Certificates & secrets → New client secret.
7.1: Give it a description and an expiry (12 or 24 months recommended; calendar a renewal task).
7.2: Copy the secret Value immediately — it is hidden after you leave the page. This is your Client Secret.

body.9: If the client secret expires, the integration silently stops refreshing tokens. Track the expiry date and rotate before it hits zero.

11.0: In the app registration → API permissions → Add a permission → Microsoft Graph → Delegated permissions.
11.1: Add: Calendars.ReadWrite, offline_access, openid, profile, User.Read.
11.2: Click "Grant admin consent for <your tenant>" so users do not have to approve each scope individually.

13.0: Calendars.ReadWrite — required to read availability and create/update events.
13.1: offline_access — required so QVO can refresh tokens without re-prompting.
13.2: openid, profile, User.Read — required for the sign-in flow and to identify the connecting user.

body.14: 4. Set the Microsoft env vars on the QVO server
body.15: QVO reads three environment variables to talk to Microsoft Graph:

16.0: MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID — the Application (client) ID from step 1.
16.1: MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET — the secret value from step 2.
16.2: MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID — which Entra tenant to authorize against (see options below).

body.17: Paste the Directory (tenant) ID from step 1 into MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID:

18.0: Single-tenant app → set MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID to your specific tenant GUID. Authorization endpoints become https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/oauth2/v2.0/...
18.1: Multi-tenant app (you let users from any org connect) → set MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID=common.
18.2: Personal Microsoft accounts only → set MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID=consumers (rare for business use).

body.19: If you self-host QVO, set MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID in your server environment. On Replit Deployments add it under Secrets. Cloud QVO tenants can request the value be set by support.

21.0: In QVO go to Integrations → Outlook Calendar → Connect.
21.1: Sign in with the Microsoft 365 account whose calendar should be used.
21.3: You return to QVO with the connector marked Connected; pick which calendar QVO may book on.

body.24: Click "Sync now" on the Outlook integration card or run a test booking flow. A new event should appear on the chosen calendar within a few seconds.

0.fix: The Redirect URI in the Entra app must exactly match the QVO callback URL, including trailing slash and protocol.

1.problem: AADSTS65001: user or admin has not consented.
1.fix: Have an Entra admin click "Grant admin consent" on the API permissions page.

2.problem: AADSTS700016: app not found in tenant.
2.fix: MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID is set to the wrong tenant. Use common for multi-tenant apps, or the right GUID for single-tenant.

3.fix: The client secret has expired or been rotated. Generate a new one in Certificates & secrets and update the QVO connector.

4.problem: Events created but not visible to others.
4.fix: Confirm the connecting user has share permissions on the target calendar, or use a shared mailbox the service account owns.

body.27: For deeper detail on Microsoft Graph auth see: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/auth-v2-user.

connecting-hubspot.title: Connecting HubSpot
connecting-hubspot.description: Create a HubSpot OAuth app (or private app) and authorize QVO to log calls and update contacts.

body.0: QVO connects to HubSpot two ways: an OAuth app (recommended for production multi-user setups) or a private app access token (fastest for a single workspace). Both require a HubSpot admin to create the app first so QVO has credentials to authorize against.
body.1: OAuth gives you per-user audit trails and refresh tokens that rotate automatically. Private apps are simpler but use one shared token that you must rotate manually.

4.0: Go to https://developers.hubspot.com → Manage apps → Create app (you may need a free developer account separate from your portal).
4.1: Under Auth, copy the Client ID and Client Secret.
4.2: Add the Redirect URL: https://app.qvo.ai/api/connectors/oauth/hubspot/callback (use your tenant's app domain if you self-host).
4.3: Under Scopes, add: crm.objects.contacts.read, crm.objects.contacts.write, crm.objects.deals.read, crm.objects.deals.write, timeline.

body.8: 2. Set the HubSpot env vars on the QVO server

9.0: HUBSPOT_CLIENT_ID — Client ID from the developer app.
9.1: HUBSPOT_CLIENT_SECRET — Client Secret from the developer app.

body.10: If you self-host QVO, set these in your server environment. On Replit Deployments add them under Secrets. Cloud QVO tenants can request the values be set by support.

12.0: In QVO go to Integrations → HubSpot → Connect.
12.1: Sign in with the HubSpot account that owns the portal QVO should write into.
12.3: You return to QVO with the connector marked Connected.

body.14: Option B — Private app access token

15.0: In HubSpot go to Settings → Integrations → Private apps → Create a private app.
15.2: Under Scopes (CRM tab) tick the same five scopes listed above.
15.3: Create the app and copy the access token (it begins with pat-).
15.4: In QVO go to Integrations → HubSpot → Connect → Use access token, and paste the token.
